topics.title: Detroit Dreams and Soupie Cells
topics.summary: During an interview, Howard discusses potential broadcasting locations including Detroit and features intern John who writes songs about himself – one titled ‘Soupie Cells’– while struggling to overcome his stuttering. The conversation then shifts to a bizarre discussion of adopted children and the reasons people might kill their parents.

topics.title: Callers Discuss Jewish Success and Racial Slurs
topics.summary: During the broadcast, callers engaged in discussions about successful individuals of Jewish descent, frequently referencing stereotypes regarding wealth and achievement while using derogatory terms such as 'coon.' The conversation included references to ‘jew boy’ and explored themes related to stuttering and attraction, alongside instances of racial slurs.

topics.title: Racial Remarks and a Problematic Theme Song
topics.summary: The broadcast features a contentious discussion centered around a theme song containing racially insensitive terms like ‘coon.’ A guest attempts to explain his creative process while grappling with the problematic lyrics, leading to arguments about listener perception and ratings. The segment concludes with an attempt to play out the entire offensive portion of the song.

topics.title: Stern & Kinison's Bon Jovi Blunder
topics.summary: During a lengthy radio segment, host Howard Stern discusses his fallout with comedian Sam Kinniston after a failed attempt to involve rock star Bon Jovi in a promotional event. He navigates listener calls and comedic tangents while ultimately agreeing to a future recording session, highlighting the awkwardness of the situation.

topics.title: FME Awards Broadcast Chaos
topics.summary: The eighth annual F.M.E awards feature Howard Stern and Robin Quivers as hosts, with a chaotic lineup of guests including Sam Kinesen, Whoopi Goldberg, Rocky Cleaver, Charles Barkley, and an Iranian man who ultimately wins an award after miscommunications. Technical difficulties and bizarre interactions punctuate the event, marked by political humor referencing Dan Quayle and Soupy Sosa.

topics.title: FME Awards Chaos and Mishaps
topics.summary: At the eighth annual FME awards, Howard Stern hosts a chaotic celebration featuring interviews with David Brenner and Mitch Fertell. Scott Muni attempts an off-key performance while interviewing Al Sharpton about George Michael and James Brown, culminating in David Brenner receiving ‘Best Mitch Interview’ after his bizarre conversation at the Super Bowl party.
